_comment: Card ownership, granted by the controller. launch_gate reads launch_block_granted
and note; a false grant with no note reads as a stub, not as a decision.
Idle is not free: a card's owner is the job still running or the one the controller
has queued, never the instantaneous nvidia-smi row.
AND A STALE GRANT IS WORSE THAN NO GRANT (b0 2026-09-03): the 0-7 grant below outlived
the run it was made for, so the next launcher would have read it as licence to take
cards 4 and 7 -- which hold the USER'S OWN work in another container. The rule above
cuts both ways: a card's owner is not the nvidia-smi row, and it is not a superseded
note: REVISED 2026-09-03: the block is cards 0-3 for the 206M data leg at world 4. The 2026-09-02 grant of ALL EIGHT cards is SUPERSEDED -- it was made for the 500M/20B run, that run is not running, and two of its eight cards are now held by the user's own tilerl and acc_spec containers. card_claim reports 4 and 7 as ORPHAN because it can see our claims and not another container's ownership; their pids are invisible to ps in this namespace, so they are not ours to read and not ours to kill. Recorded as a BOUNDARY, not as an orphan to reclaim. || The superseded grant's own text is kept below under superseded_2026_09_02 rather than deleted: it holds the costs that were accepted when the lane was given up, and the reasons a decision was taken do not stop being true when the decision is narrowed.
verified: 2026-09-03: memory_measured at world=4 is a real measurement for THIS shape, not an extrapolation from another world size and not from another model -- 61.01 GiB peak (max over 50 windows, range 60.95-61.01) at 206.1M d1024 L12 b16 accum2 seq4096 without grad_ckpt, 34.57 GiB headroom, recorded in runs/memory_peaks.json as world 4. The world=8 verification below belongs to the 493.6M L32 model and covers nothing about this leg; all three earlier peaks are that model's.

next_grant.to: the params leg (438.4M d1536 L12 h12 ffn4608 x 3.761775B tokens)
next_grant.for: the second half of the params-or-data comparison, run SERIALLY after the data leg
next_grant.blocked_on: the data leg finishing, AND a measured peak for the 438M shape -- runs/memory_peaks.json has no entry for it, and d1536 is 1.5x the width every recorded peak was measured at. Same refusal as this leg met.

cards.0-3: data leg, 206M x 8.000B, world 4 -- this grant. Free at 2026-09-03 04:59Z (0 MiB / 381 / 569 / 0; the sub-GiB rows on 1 and 2 are context, not a job).
cards.4: THE USER'S OWN WORK, in another container: tilerl grpo-gsm8k-27b (pid 3400348 in the host namespace, 41,305 MiB at 04:59Z). NEVER TAKE. It sits inside the old 0-7 grant, which is exactly why that grant had to be narrowed.
cards.7: THE USER'S OWN WORK, in another container: scripts/acc_spec_arms.py on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (pid 3179342 in the host namespace, 43,443 MiB at 04:59Z). NEVER TAKE.

lane_note: Card 7 granted as the lane at 05:52Z. It held the user's own acc_spec_arms (host pid 3179342) in another container until ~05:45Z and read 0 MiB at 05:51Z. The user's container may take it back without notice, so: read nvidia-smi before claiming, and a job here yields to a user process rather than contending. Card 4 still holds the user's grpo-gsm8k-27b and is NOT granted. Idle is not free -- this is a grant, not an inference from the nvidia-smi row.

superseded_2026_09_02.note: Granted for the 500M/20B run on ALL EIGHT cards, user ruling 2026-09-02. The lane is gone by that ruling and the cost was stated before it was taken: in-run milestone generation sweeps cannot run, because the scorer needs a whole 95 GiB card and not a gap -- observed, not derived, when the probe's scorer took card 7 alone after training exited. End-of-run scoring is unaffected: run_ddp.sh scores after torchrun exits, when all eight are free. Second cost: the 200M comparison axis loses its free pin at step 17,500 and needs 15,313 plus conversion. Both were on the table before the decision. Resume was PROVEN before this grant, per the user's order of 2026-09-02: six conditions, nine domains character-for-character, plus a reverse test that made the guard fire. --auto-resume is 1 and not more: the cursor is per-segment, so a second resume re-reads 10,240 rows and nothing has ever tested it.
